daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The government and DPR are working to revise the draft Asset Forfeiture Bill to align with the 1945 Constitution and the new Criminal Procedure Code, with DPR preparing a new draft as Minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra confirmed that the government wants the bill aligned with constitutional requirements. The DPR is also considering forming a special working committee to examine MBG governance issues after criticism emerged. Separately, Interior Minister briefed Commission II on ministry performance, highlighting corruption prevention strategies in regional governments and proposing to include spending caps for regional elections in the election law revision.

  • PDIP is taking legal action against Zulfan Lindan over allegations related to 2025 demonstration unrest, with party chair Megawati issuing instructions regarding the lawsuit.
  • The KPK declared the envelope case involving Environment Minister closed but is continuing to investigate links to the Kuantan Singingi regent.
  • KPK questioned BPK member Bobby Rizaldi for nine hours following a search of his residence, probing the arrangement of BPK audits for Muara Enim.
  • A legal expert suggested President Prabowo sent an implicit message for KPK to take over the Febrie Adriansyah case, while the Attorney General's office said KPK investigators could be involved in investigating the former special crimes director.
  • The Constitutional Court ruled that mining permit priority for mass organizations must be granted with clear parameters and not through direct appointment.
  • DPR is advancing the Archipelagic Regions Bill to correct development policies that have historically favored land-based areas over island regions.
  • Commission VIII highlighted BPK findings requiring the Social Affairs Ministry to return Rp 2 trillion in social assistance funds.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Indonesian Army is investigating an ammunition depot explosion in East Java that killed one soldier and injured six others, with TNI providing medical care and support to victims. Indonesia's Deputy Foreign Minister confirmed no Indonesian citizens were affected by the escalating US-Iran conflict and stated Indonesia continues to push conflicting parties in Myanmar toward dialogue for peace.

  • Indonesia and China launched a joint shipbuilding technology academy to enhance bilateral cooperation in maritime industrial development.
  • Indonesia and Spain reaffirmed support to protect Palestinian culture and agreed to expand collaboration in the film industry.
  • Indonesia will participate in China's AI cooperation initiative WAICO to strengthen technology partnerships.
  • Indonesian and Iranian officials explored closer labor cooperation to enhance workforce ties between the two countries.
  • The Indonesian military seized 5,000 cannabis plants in a Highland Papua raid as part of ongoing anti-narcotics operations.

Other

President Prabowo launched the Abadi Masela LNG project virtually, with the initiative expected to generate $37.8 billion in revenue and expedite eastern Indonesia's development. The president emphasized that Indonesia will prioritize domestic markets for gas supply and vowed to visit Maluku following the launch. President Prabowo also pushed for cross-sector collaboration on the free meal program implementation.

  • Indonesia cut micro-loan interest rates to eight percent to support MSMEs in accessing more affordable financing.
  • The government will make corporate packaging waste management mandatory while simplifying rules to fast-track waste-to-energy projects, as Pertamina plans to build a 30 MW waste-to-energy plant in Yogyakarta.
  • Basarnas reported that 46 passengers of KM Nurul Salsa were rescued while 23 remain missing following a maritime incident.
  • PLN is fast-tracking Bali's energy independence push to accelerate the island's transition to sustainable power sources.
  • The National Library will no longer distribute books to regions, marking a shift in its distribution policy for library materials.
